(1) microseismic event location and crack orientation are related to stress orientation, (2) microseismicity is a good indicator for the degree of damage in terms of crack length, and (3) microseismic data are useful for determining the extent of damage zone in terms of crack distribution.
Microseismicity is a valuable tool in quantifying the degree of damage in terms of crack distribution and density, and the extent of EDZ in terms of the distribution of crack density.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) the use of tensile cracking model to calculate realistic crack size from microseismic events and the application of the crack size to the calculation of crack density; (2) the determination of the crack density from microseismic data; (3) the application of the micro mechanics based constitutve model to the calculation of rock mass properties from the crack density distribution.

the microseismic event data can provide valuable insight into the dynamic rock mass properties of the EDZ, including its extent and the damage state.
a microseismicity based damage quantification approach is a valuable tool for assessing the extent of the damage zone in underground structures and for the characterization of the EDZ.
the microseismic monitoring data can be quantitively related to the damage state of the rock mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microseismic method can be used to determine the extent of the damaged zone and the degree of damage quantitatively.
the microseismic method is not only a powerful tool for locating the extent of the damage but also for quantifying the damage state of the EDZ in terms of the crack density and crack orientation.
the EDZ can be quantified in terms of crack distribution and crack density, and that the dynamic rock mass properties, including anisotropic stiffness, strength and damage, can be estimated.

microseismic event information can be used to quantify the damage state of the rock mass, and the extent of EDZ.
the microseismic method can be used to provide quantitative information on rock damage and the EDZ.
